title: Beyond Scaling: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Hardware Kernel Optimization via an Experience-Driven Workflow and Experience Graph Memory

visual_explainer.blocker: A paper-specific mechanism figure has not yet passed grounded VISUAL_POLICY.md review; the verified bilingual deep note carries the mechanism, controls, and lifecycle caveats meanwhile.

analysis.tldr: KOPE turns compiler/correctness/performance outcomes into persistent experience graph state and reuses it under a fixed context budget; same-workflow ablations show both active context management and graph memory affect later kernel decisions, but the paper still couples retrieval, compression, and injection inside the active-context mechanism.
analysis.problem: Kernel-optimization agents repeatedly discover hardware-specific strategies and failures but normally discard execution evidence after each run; replaying all trajectories is too expensive and obscures which earlier decision/outcome is useful for the current optimization state.
analysis.core_idea: Persist each optimization attempt as a journal plus structured case linked in a decision-to-outcome graph; retain positive and negative execution evidence, rank experience using relevance plus observed downstream outcomes, and actively inject a bounded warm subset before each fixed-model optimization decision.

memory_design.write: Every compile/test/profile attempt is recorded, including failed or regressing candidates, as narrative Journal plus structured Case with code change, outcome, measurements, confidence, session/step, and predecessor ids.
memory_design.organize: Cases form a directed acyclic experience forest over decision lineage and alternative branches; observed step outcome and discounted downstream outcomes are ranking heuristics, not causal labels.
memory_design.read: Active Context Management rebuilds each prompt with required hot task state plus graph-ranked warm experience and bounded cold knowledge under fixed caps, so an event from one step or task can alter later optimization decisions.
memory_design.update_forget: Memory is append/evolve oriented and persists across tasks; the paper evaluates selection under a token budget but does not establish long-horizon deletion, consolidation, privacy, or graph-maintenance governance.

compared_to: Passive agent-led context construction with the same GLM-5.2 workflow and complete 53-operator suite
The same workflow with versus without Experience Graph Memory
CANNBot and CUDA-Agent under matched models/target suite where possible
analysis.evidence: On the complete 53-operator, 1,060-case active-context ablation, pass rate rises from 60.0% (636/1,060) to 84.6% (897/1,060) while optimization tokens fall from 15.9B to 1.113B (−93.0%); score rises 636.00→2004.49. The graph-memory ablation fixes the GLM-5.2 workflow and raises full-suite pass rate from 55.2% to 84.6%; on 412 paired valid timing cases the graph-enabled variant has a 1.43× geometric-mean speedup ratio. The paper explicitly notes that active context jointly changes selection, compression, and injection.
analysis.why_it_matters: This is unusually concrete evidence that execution-grounded external memory can change future tool decisions while reducing context cost: memory value is not recall of old text but preserving decision→outcome evidence that a later optimizer can consume at the right state.
limitations: Active Context Management is an integrated ablation that co-varies retrieval ranking, context compression, and injection, so its internal credit assignment remains unresolved.
The graph's downstream-outcome score is a retrieval heuristic over observed lineage, not an identified causal contribution of an earlier optimization decision.
Primary evidence is hardware-kernel optimization on Ascend/CANN Bench; transfer to other agent domains and long-running heterogeneous stores remains open.
Token consumption is reported, but full memory construction, embedding/index, graph maintenance, storage, dollar, and energy lifecycle costs are not.
